steps: Measure the overlap in the live tab

log.msg: Cause: `.pages` is `overflow-y: scroll`, so the region always reserves a 15px gutter flush against `.app`'s content edge — which is exactly the rail's inline-start edge, where `.dev-grip` straddles. On /framework/ext/Panel/ at 2706 the gutter is 1931→1946 and the grip is 1931→1963; elementFromPoint at 1935/1940/1944/1946 all return dev-grip. The 2026-08-16 devbar-grip-offscreen fix only covered the CLOSED rail.

Decision (Mike): grip goes fully inside the rail at 12px — it fits the dead strip the rail already has (1px border + 11.52px padding on head/tabs/body), so no content moves. Rejected: widening rail padding for a 16px target; pushing .app's reservation out by half the grip. Falls out: the closed slide loses its `+ var(--dev-grip)` term.

log.msg: Verified. Mike's Chrome (2706, rail 760): scroll gutter 1931→1946, grip 1947→1959, overlap 0px — every probe across the gutter returns `pages`, none returns `dev-grip`. Closed: bar at 2706 (= innerWidth), grip 2707→2719 off screen, right-edge hits reach the page. Headless 1600 with a real mouse: grip drag took the rail 300px → 420px following the pointer exactly; closed grip 1601→1613 off screen, right-edge elementFromPoint returns page content.

Observed, not fixed: grabbing the grip snaps the rail edge to the pointer, so a grab lands up to 12px narrow (0 at the lit line, which is where you aim). The straddle had the same discontinuity at ±16px, so this is not new — grip.js is unchanged. A 3-line grab-offset would make it exact; logged in the readme's Open list rather than sunk as an unasked edit.

assign.outcome: **The page's scrollbar is reachable again.** `.pages` is `overflow-y: scroll`, so the page region always reserves a scroll gutter flush against the rail's inline-start edge — exactly where `.dev-grip` straddled at `2rem` wide. Measured on /framework/ext/Panel/ at 2706: gutter 1931→1946, grip 1931→1963, `elementFromPoint` returning `dev-grip` for every pixel of the scrollbar, with `setPointerCapture` swallowing the whole drag. There is no room on the page side of that line at all, so the grip moved wholly inside the rail: `--dev-grip: 2rem` + `translateX(-50%)` became a plain `width: 0.75rem`, landing on the dead strip the rail already had (1px border + 0.9em padding on head/tabs/body), so no content moved. Two things fell out: `devbar.css` hides with a plain `translateX(100%)` again and the `--dev-grip` token is gone, so the two files can no longer disagree about a number they no longer share. Verified — real Chrome: overlap 0px, every gutter probe returns `pages`; closed grip 2707→2719, off screen. Headless 1600 with a real mouse: the grip drag took the rail 300→420 following the pointer exactly. Cost, recorded: a 12px target where the straddle offered 32. Docs refreshed: readme.md (a new Decision + an Open note), doc/docking.md, doc/file/grip.css.md, doc/file/devbar.css.md, doc/file/grip.js.md, and four now-false comments in grip.css, grip.js and DevBar.js. All eight DevBar doc urls load clean at 1600 — no console errors, no md-error, no overflow.
